correctness.rationale: Direct proof classifies all involutions in odd characteristic, expands det(A-V), and computes all hyperplane sections of the quadric Q(V)=1. The nilpotent section and split/anisotropic sections have explicit coordinates and full cardinalities. The scalar case and the sharp minimum with exact extremizer counts follow by case analysis, including q=3. Standalone exhaustive enumeration over F3,F5,F7,F11,F9 verifies 24,309 prescribed matrices, but the proof holds for every odd prime-power q.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Theorem 2.5 of Luo et al implies equal ordinary two-unit counts at I2 and 2I2 (both rank two), but the new fibers at q=5 are respectively 1 and 32. The uniform total of involutions from 1972 also cannot determine the varying intersection with singular translates without additional geometry. Existence-only results are strictly weaker than exact multiplicity distributions.

originality.rationale: The 2025 Luo–Lei–Ji rank-only enumeration of unrestricted sums of units does not count the restricted involution summand and cannot imply a conjugacy-sensitive count (for example I and 2I over F5 have counts 1 and 32). The inspected full texts of the 1972 involution enumeration and the 2026 translation/extension establish counts of involutions or existence of decompositions but not per-matrix additive unit-plus-involution fibers. published-finding corpus semantic searches returned closely named results with fundamentally different defining operations. Residual possibility of unindexed historical equivalences remains.
residual_risks: An older equivalent expression under additive translates of orthogonal quadrics or unit/involution sums could exist outside searched databases.
No external independent mathematical audit has been conducted.

value.rationale: The unrestricted two-unit convolution in the 2025 motivating literature has rank-only fibers and cannot determine the involution-restricted decomposition problem, whose fibers vary sharply even among invertible matrices. The result supplies a complete natural exact distribution, sharp second-minimum, and identifies all extremizing matrices for infinitely many finite fields; these are mathematically useful robustness data for the involution property beyond mere existence.
